title: SAP procure to pay: suppliers, requisitions, purchase orders, purchase order history, supplier invoices
status_note: Every table, key and relationship below is taken from public documentation and written in our own words. None of it has been checked against an SAP system by this project; validate_plan checks it against your rows. A pack is a sourced suggestion, not proof.

tables.name: LFA1
tables.note: In S/4HANA suppliers are maintained as business partners; LFA1 is still the supplier table that purchasing documents point at.

tables.name: EBAN
tables.note: A requisition has no header table of its own: BANFN groups the items.

tables.name: EKKO
tables.note: Purchase orders, contracts and scheduling agreements share this table; BSTYP and BSART tell them apart.

tables.name: EKPO
tables.note: The currency of the item's net value is the header's WAERS. LOEKZ marks deleted items, which stay in the table.

tables.name: EKET
tables.note: Several schedule lines per item: a join of EKPO and EKET repeats the item's NETWR once per schedule line.

tables.name: EKBE
tables.note: One row per event on an order item: goods receipts, invoices, reversals. VGABE says which kind; SHKZG says the direction, and amounts are unsigned.

tables.name: RBKP
tables.note: BELNR here is the invoice document number, from another number range than the accounting document's BELNR in BKPF; the two meet only through BKPF.AWKEY.

relationships.condition: Requisitions for services or free-text items leave MATNR empty.
Service and free-text items leave MATNR empty.
Only items created from a requisition; the others leave BANFN empty.
History rows of invoice receipts (VGABE '2'); for goods receipts BELNR is a material document, another number range.
Items without a material leave MATNR empty.
A purchasing organization that buys for several company codes leaves BUKRS empty.

traps.title: MANDT in every join, here too
traps.text: Every procure-to-pay table starts its key with the client; the pack's keys and relationships carry it.

traps.title: The purchase order history multiplies order items
traps.text: EKBE has a row per goods receipt, invoice and reversal of an order item. Summing EKPO.NETWR over a join with EKBE counts the item once per event (Krusgraph's 'the total that doubles' check names it). Aggregate EKBE per item first, and use VGABE and SHKZG: amounts are unsigned and reversals are rows of their own.

traps.title: The invoice's gross amount sits on the header
traps.text: RBKP.RMWWR is the gross amount of the whole supplier invoice, RSEG.WRBTR that of one item. Summing RMWWR over RSEG rows counts each invoice once per item.

traps.title: Two different BELNR
traps.text: RBKP.BELNR is the invoice document number; BKPF.BELNR is the accounting document number, from another number range. Joining them on BELNR (and BUKRS, GJAHR, which RBKP also has) matches unrelated documents. The accounting document points back through BKPF.AWTYP and AWKEY, a key built from the invoice number and year; the pack names that link but does not apply it.

traps.title: Document numbers repeat across fiscal years
traps.text: RBKP, RSEG and EKBE carry GJAHR in the key: an invoice number is unique only within its year. A join without GJAHR pairs invoices of different years.

traps.title: Deleted order items stay in EKPO
traps.text: EKPO.LOEKZ marks deleted or blocked items. They stay in the table and in a sum unless filtered.
